title: Bram and the Songbook
premise: Mara Nakamura inherited her grandmother's vineyard along with its crushing debts, and the only thing keeping her afloat is a lucrative contract with a wine conglomerate that wants her land. When her family reunion demands she arrive with a partner, she hires Bram Okafor, a charming session musician who plays weddings for cash, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date turns real by dessert, but Bram's sister works for the very conglomerate buying Mara's vineyard, and his testimony in an ongoing dispute could either save or sink her. As Mara discovers the contract hides a clause that would raze her grandmother's vines, she must choose between signing the deal that saves everything and trusting Bram, whose loyalty to his family collides with the truth he owes her; they end by tearing up the deal together, saving the vineyard through a community co-op, and admitting the love that stopped being pretend long ago.
about_author: Silas Pemberton is the pen name of a former sommelier turned novelist who spent a decade pouring wine in the Willamette Valley before trading corkscrews for keyboards. They write warm, slow-burn romances about people rebuilding lives from ruins.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She surveys the vineyard at dawn, cataloguing debts like frost damage, then opens a letter from Halcyon Wine Group renewing their purchase offer. Her accountant warns time is short. Emotional beat: weary pragmatism masking grief for the grandmother whose dream she's mortgaging.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her mother calls: the family reunion will celebrate her cousin's engagement, and everyone expects Mara to explain why she's still alone and still failing. Panic drives her to a classified ad for hired companions. Emotional beat: humiliation curdling into reckless resolve.

chapters.title: A Man Who Plays Weddings
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Introduced mid-gig, playing love songs at a stranger's wedding while privately cynical about romance since his divorce and custody struggles. He answers Mara's ad because he needs rent money. Emotional beat: guarded charm hiding loneliness.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. Over coffee, they negotiate rules: no real names of exes, no touching beyond hand-holding, one weekend only. Bram notices Mara flinch when discussing her family. Emotional beat: transactional distance already fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: Arrival at Hollow Creek
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The reunion begins at her aunt's estate; Bram performs effortless warmth, charming her skeptical uncle with stories. Mara watches him work and feels something unwanted stir. Emotional beat: surprise at how easy pretending feels.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. During toasts, Mara's father publicly mocks her vineyard failures; Bram abandons script and defends her with fierce sincerity. Later, on the porch, the pretense dissolves into a first real kiss. Emotional beat: the fake date becoming dangerously true.

chapters.title: Sunday Morning Rules
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Waking tangled together, they awkwardly renegotiate: the weekend is over but neither wants it to be. They agree to keep seeing each other, honestly this time. Emotional beat: tentative hope shadowed by secrets unshared.

chapters.title: What Bram Didn't Mention
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Revealed: his sister Adaeze is Halcyon's regional acquisitions manager, and Bram has agreed to give a deposition about Mara's vineyard operations in Halcyon's dispute with a neighboring grower. Guilt keeps him silent with Mara. Emotional beat: complicity tightening.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Bram starts helping with harvest, bonding with her ragtag crew of misfit workers—her found family. He learns the vines' history from her grandmother's songbook of field lullabies. Emotional beat: belonging he didn't seek.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Warning
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. His sister confronts him: if his deposition favors the neighbor, Halcyon retaliates against both him and Mara's contract. If it favors Halcyon, the neighboring farm dies. She invokes family loyalty. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: The Clause
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Reading the renewed contract line by line, Mara finds a hidden clause granting Halcyon demolition rights over the original vines—the ones tied to her grandmother's legacy. Her lawyer confirms there's no way out once signed. Emotional beat: cold dread.

chapters.title: Songbook Nights
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Bram sets her grandmother's lullabies to music as a gift; they share a near-perfect evening. Mara almost tells him about the clause but stops herself, testing trust she isn't sure exists. Emotional beat: intimacy built on withheld truth.

chapters.title: Deposition Day
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Under oath, Bram must choose. He testifies truthfully, damaging Halcyon's case—and his sister's career. Walking out, he calls Mara to confess everything, but she doesn't answer. Emotional beat: integrity purchased at terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Before Bram can reach her, Mara receives an anonymous photo of Bram entering Halcyon headquarters weeks ago. Confronting him that night, she hears his confession as betrayal, not courage. She tells him to leave. Emotional beat: trust shattering on a technicality of timing.

chapters.title: Empty Rows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Alone during harvest, Mara realizes the crew misses Bram too—that he'd woven himself into her found family. Her mother, unexpectedly, urges her not to repeat her own marriage's silence. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into clarity.

chapters.title: Sister to Sister
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV (single chapter). Adaeze visits Mara, revealing Bram's full sacrifice: the deposition, the estrangement from her, the job offers he refused. She delivers Bram's notebook of songs written for Mara. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance between wounded women.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Deadline
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Halcyon, stung by the deposition, gives Mara 48 hours to sign or lose the payment that clears her debts. Her lawyer says sign; her heart says burn it. Emotional beat: the choice compressed to two days.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Songbook
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram returns during the harvest festival, and before the whole community, plays the finished songbook—her grandmother's melodies made whole. Publicly, he lays out every truth: the contract, the clause, his failure. Emotional beat: love declared without guarantee.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara refuses to sign, gambling everything on a desperate alternative: converting the vineyard to a community co-op with her crew, neighbors—including the farmer Halcyon was destroying—and Adaeze's insider knowledge of Halcyon's legal weaknesses. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: Climax: The Vote
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the co-op vote, Halcyon makes a final hostile bid; Bram's truthful deposition becomes the legal linchpin that voids their claim. The community votes yes. Mara and Bram reconcile amid the celebration, choosing each other with eyes open. Emotional beat: triumph earned collectively.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Months later: first co-op vintage bottled, labeled with a line from the songbook. Bram has moved his piano into the tasting room. Small safe steps, now taken together. Emotional beat: quiet, durable joy.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Epilogue, both POVs braided. One year on, at the next family reunion—held at the vineyard—Bram proposes where they first kissed, using a melody from the songbook. Mara's answer is a kiss before he finishes asking. Emotional beat: the pretend made permanent.
